research_question: Can the already-frozen dense T-24..T-1 sequence shape improve ordinary H/D/A argmax when it learns class-specific residuals around the T-1 market probabilities instead of predicting draw-vs-nondraw and inheriting a fixed H:A split?

source_and_feature_binding.core_bookmakers: same fixed all-hours T-24..T-1 core bookmaker set as R39E

population.fourth100_selection_rule: same sha256('51139|' + identity) ordering; zero-based ranks [300,400)

market_offset.source: frozen R39C T-1h de-vig consensus q=(qH,qD,qA)

model.features: 25 frozen R39E dense sequence features only
equations: eta_H = log(qH/qA) + beta_H0 + z dot beta_H
eta_D = log(qD/qA) + beta_D0 + z dot beta_D
model.l2_penalty: all feature slopes for H and D; no penalty on intercepts
model.optimizer: full-batch Newton-Raphson with exact 2-block multinomial Hessian and backtracking line search
model.decision_rule: ordinary argmax of the final H/D/A probabilities

planned_comparators_on_fourth100: R39E frozen binary 40-feature dense sequence model

planned_gates.probability_signal: R39F log_loss, brier and rps strictly better than R39E; draw_auc strictly better than market
planned_gates.decision_increment: R39F accuracy strictly better than market, R39C and R39E; predicted draws >=1; draw_f1 strictly better than R39E
planned_gates.strong_uncertainty: match-date cluster-bootstrap p05 for R39F minus market accuracy >0
